rulebaseSources: UK Health and Safety at Work Act 1974

turnaroundRequirements.makeupIntensiveTurnaround: 14-hour minimum for lead performers after extensive makeup application (e.g., 'Ape' characters, aging makeup).
turnaroundRequirements.stuntPerformers: 12-hour minimum, 14-hour after high-risk work (e.g., 'Zero-G' sequences, animal interaction).
turnaroundRequirements.nightToDayTurnaround: 12-hour minimum for all cast and crew when transitioning from a night shoot (wrap after midnight) to a day shoot (call before 7 AM).

mealBreakRequirements.firstMeal: Mandatory 30-minute break required within 6 hours of call time.
mealBreakRequirements.secondMeal: Mandatory 30-minute break required within 12 hours of call time.
mealBreakRequirements.penalties: Triggered if break is not provided within 6.5 hours (first meal) or 12.5 hours (second meal).

overtimeRegulations.standardDay: Up to 10 hours at straight time.
overtimeRegulations.goldenTime: Hours beyond 16 paid at a premium rate, often negotiated per union agreement.
overtimeRegulations.stuntPerformers: 8-hour straight time day, with overtime calculations starting after the 8th hour.
overtimeRegulations.weekendPremiums: Saturday work at 1.5x, Sunday work at 2.0x.
overtimeRegulations.nightPremium: 25% uplift for work between 8 PM and 6 AM.

childActorRestrictions.workingHours: Strictly limited by age (e.g., 4.5 hours/day for ages 8-11).
childActorRestrictions.onSetRequirements: Mandatory presence of parent/guardian, welfare officer, and tutor if applicable.

animalWelfareRequirements.applicability: All scenes involving live animals or performers in realistic animal costumes ('Dawn of Man').
animalWelfareRequirements.supervision: Certified veterinarian and/or RSPCA/local equivalent representative on set.
animalWelfareRequirements.handlers: Level 3 certified handlers required for all animal interactions.
animalWelfareRequirements.workLimits: Minimum 2-hour rest period every 4 hours of work.
animalWelfareRequirements.environmentalControls: No work permitted in temperatures below 10°C or above 32°C.

stuntSafetyProtocols.applicability: All scenes involving 'Zero-G' effects, animal interaction, or other high-risk physical activity.
stuntSafetyProtocols.personnel: IATSE-certified Stunt Coordinator and on-set Safety Officer are mandatory.
stuntSafetyProtocols.medical: Paramedic standby required for all high-risk stunts.
stuntSafetyProtocols.rehearsal: Minimum of 3 full rehearsals before filming any stunt sequence.
stuntSafetyProtocols.engineering: Mechanical rigs (e.g., centrifuge, 'Zero-G' wires) require certified engineer sign-off.

foreignLocationRegulations.workPermits: Minimum 21 working day processing time. Must be initiated well in advance.
foreignLocationRegulations.localCrew: Minimum 60% local crew hiring requirement must be met.
foreignLocationRegulations.specialPermissions: Separate labor office approval required for any planned weekend or night work.

hardConstraints.description: Minimum 12-hour turnaround for lead performers, 14-hour after heavy makeup/stunts.
hardConstraints.violation: Union grievance, forced call (production shutdown), significant financial penalties (day's pay per hour of violation).

hardConstraints.description: Minimum 10-hour turnaround for general crew, 11-hour for department heads.
First meal break must be provided within 6 hours of call time.
hardConstraints.violation: Mandatory financial penalties for every 30-minute delay.

hardConstraints.description: A certified Stunt Coordinator and Safety Officer must be on set for all stunt sequences.
hardConstraints.violation: Production insurance invalidation, legal liability for injury, immediate shutdown by union/safety reps.

hardConstraints.description: Animal work is prohibited in temperatures above 32°C or below 10°C.
hardConstraints.violation: Legal action from animal welfare groups, permit revocation, severe reputational damage.

hardConstraints.description: Foreign national cast/crew cannot work without a valid, processed work permit.
applicableTo: All non-Namibian cast/crew working in Namibia
hardConstraints.violation: Deportation, fines, blacklisting of production company in the country.

softConstraints.description: Limit consecutive work days to a maximum of 6 before a mandatory 24-hour rest day.
softConstraints.violation: Increased risk of crew fatigue, accidents, and burnout. Potential for premium pay on 7th day.
softConstraints.penalty: BECTU/SAG 7th day premium pay; decreased productivity.

softConstraints.description: Minimize scheduling on Saturdays and especially Sundays to avoid premium overtime pay.
softConstraints.violation: Significant budget impact due to 1.5x Saturday and 2.0x Sunday pay rates.

softConstraints.description: Cluster scenes requiring heavy makeup ('Ape', 'Aging') on consecutive days to manage performer turnaround and makeup artist scheduling.
softConstraints.violation: Inefficient use of makeup department; scheduling conflicts due to extended 14-hour turnarounds.
softConstraints.penalty: Increased holding days for makeup artists; potential for idle cast/crew.

softConstraints.description: Schedule Namibian exterior shoots during the dry season to minimize weather delays.
softConstraints.violation: High probability of shooting days lost to rain, impacting budget and schedule.
softConstraints.penalty: Cost of weather-hold days for entire location unit.

mealPenalties.structure: Calculated in 30-minute increments. First 30-min delay after 6-hour mark: 1.5x rate. Subsequent delays escalate per union agreement.
mealPenalties.example: A crew member on $50/hr missing a meal break pays a penalty starting at $25 for the first half-hour violation.

overtimePenalties.structure: Time-and-a-half (1.5x) for hours 10-14, Double-time (2.0x) for hours 14-16. Stunt OT begins after 8 hours.
overtimePenalties.example: A 15-hour day for a crew member on $50/hr costs $675 (10x$50 + 4x$75 + 1x$100), excluding night premiums.

turnaroundPenalties.structure: Forced call violation typically results in a penalty of one day's pay for the affected individual for each hour of infringement.
turnaroundPenalties.example: Giving a lead actor 10 hours turnaround instead of 12 (2-hour infringement) could cost two full daily salaries as a penalty.

complianceRecommendations.recommendation: Immediately begin the work permit application process for all non-Namibian cast and key crew for the 'Dawn of Man' sequence. Allow for a minimum of 30 working days.
complianceRecommendations.impactIfIgnored: Inability to shoot in Namibia, forcing a costly and creatively compromising relocation.

complianceRecommendations.recommendation: Secure and contract an IATSE-certified Stunt Coordinator and a certified Animal Wrangler/Handler before any stunt or animal scene scheduling.
complianceRecommendations.impactIfIgnored: Violation of safety regulations, invalidation of insurance, extreme risk of injury or death.

complianceRecommendations.recommendation: Explicitly flag all 'Ape' and 'Aging' makeup days in the schedule and automatically apply the 14-hour turnaround constraint to all affected performers for the following day.
complianceRecommendations.impactIfIgnored: Systemic turnaround violations, leading to significant financial penalties and crew fatigue.

complianceRecommendations.recommendation: Build a significant contingency fund (at least 15% of labor budget) specifically for overtime and meal penalties, as the project's complexity makes violations highly probable.
complianceRecommendations.impactIfIgnored: Severe budget overruns in the latter stages of production.

riskAssessment.description: Delay or rejection of Namibian work permits for key cast or crew.
riskAssessment.impact: Entire 'Dawn of Man' sequence delayed or cancelled, requiring a complete production rethink.
riskAssessment.mitigation: Engage a reputable local fixer in Namibia immediately. Submit applications with extensive lead time and have backup personnel identified.

riskAssessment.description: Injury to cast or crew during complex 'Zero-G' wirework or animal interaction stunts.
riskAssessment.impact: Serious injury/death, production shutdown, legal investigation, and massive insurance claims.
riskAssessment.mitigation: Strict adherence to all stunt safety protocols, extensive rehearsals, and empowerment of the Stunt Coordinator and Safety Officer to halt any unsafe activity.

riskAssessment.description: Systemic turnaround violations due to scheduling pressure and long makeup times.
riskAssessment.impact: Accumulation of massive financial penalties. Severe crew and cast fatigue leading to on-set errors and safety incidents.
riskAssessment.mitigation: Use scheduling software that automates and enforces turnaround constraints. The 1st AD must prioritize compliance over speed.

riskAssessment.description: Unseasonal weather in Namibia disrupts the exterior 'Dawn of Man' shoot.
riskAssessment.impact: Multiple expensive weather-hold days where the full cast and crew are on standby.
riskAssessment.mitigation: Schedule the shoot deep within the historical dry season. Have alternate, interior scenes ready to shoot as a backup.

nextStepRecommendations: Dispatch to Resource Logistics Agent to source and confirm availability of certified Stunt Coordinator, Animal Handlers, and Namibian-based crew.
Initiate work permit application process for Namibia immediately based on a preliminary shooting schedule.
Provide generated hard and soft constraints to the Optimization & Scenario Agent for schedule modeling.
Request detailed cast and crew list from production office to finalize union categorizations and applicability of all rules.
